key_insight: SLiR makes linear relaxations for neural-network activations broadly optimizable by computing sound bounds through slope-based shifting, rather than relying on activation-specific hand-crafted formulas.
engineering_relevance: This reduces manual effort when verifying modern neural networks and helps formal methods scale to new activation functions used in safety- and security-critical systems.
method: Parameterize each relaxation by its slope.
Compute the offset with a shifting procedure to preserve sound upper and lower bounds.
Use only a Lipschitz constant or critical points to support general activation functions.
evidence_signal: Experiments in the abstract report tight relaxations across many practical activation functions and up to 7.8x more verifiable properties than state-of-the-art methods.
watch_item: The approach still depends on correctly obtaining a valid Lipschitz constant or critical points, and soundness can be compromised if these inputs are inaccurate.
paper_title: Shifting-based Optimizable Linear Relaxations for General Activation Functions
